answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may post trades or earn rewards. Peers accept only actions backed by that on-chain stake; when an identity double-spends or violates agreed rules, a verifier proves it and the deposit is burned. Splitting one account into a ripple of aliases therefore does not multiply influence: every alias needs fresh capital, and coordinated abuse risks losing it. A spiral of costly retries can drain the attacker, while honest agents keep their stake; willow-thin identities gain no weight for free.
